panels.description: Every validator's worker-0 observes the replicated commit sequence, so the total is the maximum worker-0 rate rather than a committee-wide sum, which would inflate TPS by committee size.
panels.title: Committed TPS (total)

panels.description: Every validator's worker-0 observes the replicated commit sequence, so the total is the maximum worker-0 byte rate rather than a committee-wide sum.
panels.title: Committed bytes rate (total)

panels.description: One line per validator's worker-0 metrics endpoint. The node label names that validator and worker directly; no committee-wide sum is applied.
panels.title: Committed TPS per node

panels.description: Submission-to-ordering cumulative p50 for each validator's worker-0 endpoint. clamp_max bounds the plot at 1,000 ms; a line on the ceiling may represent a larger raw value.
panels.title: Ordering latency per node (p50/p90/p99, ms)

panels.description: Submission-to-ordering-and-local-payload cumulative p50 for each validator's worker-0 endpoint. clamp_max bounds the plot at 1,000 ms; a line on the ceiling may represent a larger raw value.
panels.title: Materialized latency per node (p50/p90/p99, ms)
Seal routes (rate by route) -- Vantage only

panels.description: vantage_entered_view is a gauge (the highest view entered so far), not a counter -- rate() on it is meaningless, so refId A reads it directly rather than wrapping it in rate().
panels.title: View entry / seal / anchor rates
Frontier a_i / control delivered-log len / consume pos

panels.description: bytes_sent_total is genuinely additive across processes; committed_bytes is replicated, so the denominator uses the maximum validator worker-0 counter rather than summing the committee.
panels.title: Overhead bytes per sequenced byte

panels.description: bytes_sent_total is genuinely additive across processes; committed_transactions is replicated, so the denominator uses the maximum validator worker-0 rate rather than summing the committee.
panels.title: Bandwidth efficiency (512B-normalized)

panels.description: submitted_transactions is client-side and additive; committed_transactions is replicated, so committed/s uses the maximum validator worker-0 rate rather than summing the committee.
panels.title: Submitted vs. sequenced (committed) transactions/s

panels.description: Per-validator CPU used by its standalone primary and worker processes, expressed as percent of one logical core and excluding the client load generator. Values may exceed 100% when a validator uses multiple cores. Available on Linux process deployments; intentionally absent from the single-process local-benchmark.
panels.title: CPU usage (per node)

panels.description: Per-validator resident memory summed across its standalone primary and worker processes, excluding the client load generator. Available on Linux process deployments; intentionally absent from the single-process local-benchmark.
panels.title: Memory usage (per node)
